chapter: Opinions, Edgar Battle and closing stories
title: Students today and the revival of older players

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Do the students that you go to Capital with, is this basically what you tell them?

Yes, it's on that, that's the principle of it and you tell them that, of course some of them are very open minded and they appreciate the things. A lot of these young kids, they don't like a lot of these modern drummers, you know, they'll go way back and get some of Gene Krupa's

albums, Ray McKinley, Ray Baudac, go back and get some of those things, Jo Jones, they like that style. A lot of those young drummers don't like a Max Roach or Elvin Jones or like that you know. Some of them do, you know, but a lot of them don't.

There seems to have been a revival in the past few years. A lot of the players who came up, you know, before bebop and who were kind of neglected for a number of years, like Arnett Cobb. Is working a lot again.
Tenor player. Very good tenor player. Used to be with Hamp.
Right yeah. And he's working a lot again and Panama Francis has that revival of the Savoy Sultans is working a lot. George Kelly as a matter of fact.
Yeah George Kelly, they're all hometown boys. Out of Florida ... So is Al Cooper. He's out of Florida, the one who originated the Savoy Sultan. Al Cooper and the Savoy Sultans.
